Compare OsteoCar references

Stephanie J. Spielman

2026-08-05

There are several different references in OsteoCar, and while we can generally map them to our sample propertoes, we have some sample which don’t neatly line up. For example, OsteoCar has patient primary and metastatic (lung only) references, but we have a sample from metastatic tissue in bone which differs from the metastatic reference.

The goal of this notebook is to lightly compare some of the references using SingleR: * patient primary vs metastatic (lung only) references * xenograft primary vs metastatic references

We compare the references to one another to see how similar the cell type distributions and expression signatures are. As these references are quite large, they have to be aggregated before use, but we’ll also explore their raw data too.

Setup

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(SingleR)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
})
Warning: package 'SingleR' was built under R version 4.4.1
Warning: package 'SummarizedExperiment' was built under R version 4.4.1

bp_param <- BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(6)
set.seed(2026)
repository_base <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::is_git_root)

module_dir <- file.path(repository_base, "analyses", "cell-type-osteosarcoma")
ref_dir <- file.path(module_dir, "references")

Functions

make_barplot <- function(prim_coldata, mets_coldata, facet = TRUE) {
    
  prim_table <- prim_coldata |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::count(Ann_Level1, Ann_Level2) |>
    dplyr::mutate(ref = "primary")
  
  full_table <- mets_coldata |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::count(Ann_Level1, Ann_Level2) |>
    dplyr::mutate(ref = "metastasis") |>
    dplyr::bind_rows(prim_table) |>
    dplyr::group_by(ref) |>
    dplyr::mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()
  
  p_counts <- ggplot(full_table) + 
    aes(x = Ann_Level2, y = n, fill = ref) + 
    geom_col(position = position_dodge()) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
    ggtitle("Counts") +
    theme_bw() + 
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
  
  p_props <- ggplot(full_table) + 
    aes(x = Ann_Level2, y = prop, fill = ref) + 
    geom_col(position = position_dodge()) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
    ggtitle("Proportions") +
    theme_bw() + 
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
  
  if (facet) {
    p_counts <- p_counts + facet_wrap(vars(Ann_Level1), scales = "free", nrow=3)
    p_props <- p_props + facet_wrap(vars(Ann_Level1), scales = "free", nrow=3)
  }
  
  list(p_counts, p_props)
  
}

Patient reference analysis

Read references

We’ll read in and aggregate, extract colData so we can ditch these objects as soon as possible.

patient_prim <- readr::read_rds(file.path(ref_dir, "patient_prim_sce.rds"))
patient_prim_aggr <- SingleR::trainSingleR(
  ref = patient_prim,
  labels = patient_prim$Ann_Level2,
  de.method = "wilcox",
  aggr.ref = TRUE,
  BPPARAM = bp_param
)
prim_coldata <- colData(patient_prim)
rm(patient_prim)


patient_mets <- readr::read_rds(file.path(ref_dir, "patient_mets_sce.rds"))
patient_mets_aggr <- SingleR::trainSingleR(
  ref = patient_mets,
  labels = patient_mets$Ann_Level2,
  de.method = "wilcox",
  aggr.ref = TRUE,
  BPPARAM = bp_param
)
mets_coldata <- colData(patient_mets)
rm(patient_mets)

Reference cell types

First, where do cell type labels overlap or not?

The primary reference uniquely has these cell types, both of which are mesenchymal:

setdiff(
  unique(prim_coldata$Ann_Level2), unique(mets_coldata$Ann_Level2)
)
[1] "Osteoblasts"  "Chondrocytes"
Osteoblasts
Chondrocytes

The metastasis reference uniquely has these cell types, across several categories.

setdiff(
  unique(mets_coldata$Ann_Level2), unique(prim_coldata$Ann_Level2)
)
[1] "Fibroblasts"      "Alv_Macrophages"  "Epithelial_cells"
Fibroblasts
Alv_Macrophages
Epithelial_cells

The majority of cell types, including all classes of tumor cells, appear to be shared, but this does not guarantee they have similar expression.

shared <- intersect(
  unique(mets_coldata$Ann_Level2), unique(prim_coldata$Ann_Level2)
)
shared

 [4] "T_cells"           "NK_cells"          "B_cells"          
 [7] "TAMs"              "Mast"              "DC"               
[10] "Monocytes"         "Endothelial_cells" "Basal_Progenitor" 
[13] "Fibrogenic"        "MP_Progenitor"     "Proliferative"    
[16] "Interactive"       "COMA"

We’ll visualize this as well with barplots, faceted by cell type category, of cell type counts and proportions for these references for complementary views on their distributions.

make_barplot(prim_coldata, mets_coldata) |>
  wrap_plots(ncol=2, guides = "collect")

We see:

  • Relatively more endothelial in mets, and no epithelial in primary
  • Same immune lymphoid cell types but primary has relatively more T cells in the reference
  • Similar immune myeloid distributions but primary has relatively more TAMs
  • Most differences fall out in the mesenchymal cell types
  • Same sets of tumor cells, but some different enrichments between references

Heatmap

We’ll make a heatmap comparing expression across references.

We’ll compare Ann_Level2 between primary and metastatic references by first aggregating them and then running SingleR::matchReferences() and plotting the resulting heatmap. This will tell us where cell type expression patterns overlap/differ between references.

matched <- matchReferences(
  patient_mets_aggr$ref, 
  patient_prim_aggr$ref, 
  patient_mets_aggr$labels$full, 
  patient_prim_aggr$labels$full 
)

First, we’ll show all cell types:

pheatmap::pheatmap(
  matched, 
  col=viridis::magma(500), 
  cluster_rows = FALSE, 
  cluster_cols = FALSE
)

Now, only the cell types shared between the references:

shared_matched <- matched[shared, shared]
pheatmap::pheatmap(
  shared_matched, 
  col=viridis::magma(500), 
  cluster_rows = FALSE, 
  cluster_cols = FALSE
)

It is clear that while most cell type labels are in both references, many of them have distinct expression patterns. Aside from TAMs, immune cells appear largely consistent, but many of the tumor cells are not (COMA, Interactive, MP_progenitor, Fibrogenic). But, even cell types with a clearly visible diagnoal are not necessarily the highest on the color scale, which suggests differences are common. This means if we were to combine references, we want to still distinguish cell types by their source.

Xenograft reference analysis

Next, we’ll do the same analysis with xenograft references. Note that there are many fewer cell types here, because the reference considers only human-derived tumor cells. Ann_Level<0/1> are the same (all “Tumor”) and Ann_Level<2/3> are the same for the xenograft references, so Ann_Level2 is the most fine-grained we can achieve.

Read references

We’ll read in and aggregate, extract colData so we can ditch these objects as soon as possible.

xeno_prim <- readr::read_rds(file.path(ref_dir, "xeno_prim_sce.rds"))
xeno_prim_aggr <- SingleR::trainSingleR(
  ref = xeno_prim,
  labels = xeno_prim$Ann_Level2,
  de.method = "wilcox",
  aggr.ref = TRUE,
  BPPARAM = bp_param
)
prim_coldata <- colData(xeno_prim)
rm(xeno_prim)


xeno_mets <- readr::read_rds(file.path(ref_dir, "xeno_mets_sce.rds"))
xeno_mets_aggr <- SingleR::trainSingleR(
  ref = xeno_mets,
  labels = xeno_mets$Ann_Level2,
  de.method = "wilcox",
  aggr.ref = TRUE,
  BPPARAM = bp_param
)
mets_coldata <- colData(xeno_mets)
rm(xeno_mets)

Reference cell types

What are the cell types within each reference? We’ll again make barplots of the counts and proportions for complementary views; there are few enough cell types that we don’t need a table.

make_barplot(prim_coldata, mets_coldata) |>
  wrap_plots(ncol=2, guides = "collect")

Distributions are not terribly different, though the primary reference has a bit more basal progenitor and fibrogenic cells, and the metastasis reference has more mp progenitor stressed cells. Interactive and proliferative have similar proportions.

Heatmap

Now we’ll compare expression patterns of the cell types, which have the same labels in both references.

matched <- matchReferences(
  xeno_mets_aggr$ref, 
  xeno_prim_aggr$ref, 
  xeno_mets_aggr$labels$full, 
  xeno_prim_aggr$labels$full 
)
pheatmap::pheatmap(
  matched, 
  col=viridis::magma(500), 
  cluster_rows = FALSE, 
  cluster_cols = FALSE
)

There’s a 1:1 match of proliferative here only, but the noise around other cell types suggests that there are distinct expression profiles between shared cell types across these references. What is not clear is how much of that is signal vs noise. The Interactive profile also appears to be completely distinct between these, which is not inconsistent with the fact that this is the least frequent cell type in both references.

Conclusions

Given the differences between primary/metastasis references for both patients and xenografts, it seems worth doing some initial exploration of annotation performance with SingleR next.
